Buyers add at least two FIDO2 keys; on a new device they tap or insert a registered key instead of a six-digit verification code or trusted-device approval. System account behavior — outside AppLocale scope.

Security Keys vs Passkeys vs SMS 2FA — hard disambiguation

Apple and indie teams conflate three authentication stories. AppLocale covers physical FIDO Security Keys for Apple ID listing metadata — not the other features:

  • Apple ID Security Keys (this page) — physical FIDO2 / WebAuthn hardware keys registered under Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication → Security Keys; add at least two keys; tap a key on new-device Apple ID sign-in instead of a six-digit code or trusted device. Gallery frames may show Add Security Key, YubiKey or Titan compatibility, or hardware second-factor badges. zh-Hans terms: 安全密钥, 安全金钥, 添加安全密钥, Apple ID 安全密钥, FIDO 安全密钥.
  • Passkeys (different) — passwordless credentials saved in iCloud Keychain; Sign in with a passkey, Create a passkey, and passwordless login marketing. Covered on our Passkeys guide — not physical hardware you plug in or tap for Apple ID 2FA.
  • SMS / trusted-device 2FA (different — see dedicated page) — six-digit verification codes on a trusted device or approval prompts for Apple Account sign-in under Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication. General Apple Account 2FA marketing — trusted devices, verification codes, Turn On Two-Factor Authentication — is covered on our Two-Factor Authentication guide — not hardware FIDO keys.
  • Sign in with Apple (different) — Continue with Apple and Hide My Email login badges. Covered on our Sign in with Apple guide — not Apple ID Security Key registration.
  • Passwords app saved logins (related context only) — credential vault marketing may sit beside security apps, but Security Keys listing copy should focus on hardware FIDO second factor for Apple ID — not saved-password AutoFill as the lead unless your English source already claims that accurately. See Passwords listing when vault fill is your hero.

A hardware-key badge is not a passkey creation sheet, not an SMS code entry field, and not a Sign in with Apple button unless that is what the screenshot shows.

Security Keys vs Advanced Data Protection, Stolen Device Protection, and Contact Key Verification

Apple groups several account and device security toggles across Settings. Indie teams conflate them on one product page. AppLocale covers Security Keys listing metadata only — link to contrast pages when buyers need disambiguation:

  • Advanced Data Protection for iCloud (different) — end-to-end encryption for most iCloud data categories under Settings → Apple Account → iCloud → Advanced Data Protection. Separate iCloud security story — not hardware FIDO keys for Apple ID sign-in. See Advanced Data Protection listing when that is your lead feature.
  • Stolen Device Protection (different) — optional theft hardening under Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Stolen Device Protection — 失窃设备保护 and 安全延迟 vocabulary — not FIDO hardware key registration. See Stolen Device Protection listing when that is your lead feature.
  • Contact Key Verification (different) — iMessage contact-key alerts under Settings → Apple Account → Contact Key Verification — 联系人密钥验证 vocabulary — not Apple ID Security Keys. See Contact Key Verification listing when that is your lead feature.
  • Lockdown Mode, Private Relay, Hide My Email (different) — separate Settings paths with unrelated buyer vocabulary. Do not keyword-stuff those terms when English only markets Security Keys.

Security-conscious apps may mention several Apple hardening features across one description — but each gallery frame and keyword should match the feature the screenshot actually shows. A YubiKey registration overlay is not an Advanced Data Protection toggle walkthrough.

What Apple ID Security Keys actually do — listing honesty

Apple lets Apple ID accounts register physical FIDO2 security keys as a second factor for sign-in. Under Settings → [your name] → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication → Security Keys, buyers add at least two keys — then on a new device they can tap or insert a registered key instead of entering a six-digit verification code or approving from a trusted device. Third-party apps may complement this by educating buyers, documenting compatible key brands, or aligning security UX with hardware second-factor workflows. Security Key–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

Hardware-key marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Apple ID Security Keys — not a literal paste of US marketing:

设置 → [你的姓名] → 登录与安全性 → 双重认证 → 安全密钥 (添加安全密钥)

Apple's Chinese Settings path is 设置 → [你的姓名] → 登录与安全性 → 双重认证 → 安全密钥, with the registration action labeled 添加安全密钥. Screenshot walkthroughs and caption lines should mirror that path — not English "Sign-In & Security" badges alone, not 面容 ID 与密码 (Stolen Device Protection), and not iCloud (Advanced Data Protection). AppLocale uses the labels buyers see on a zh-Hans iPhone when your English gallery shows the Security Keys toggle or Add Security Key sheet.

安全密钥 vs 安全金钥

Apple's system UI uses 安全密钥 for the feature name under 双重认证. Some security marketing also uses 安全金钥 when emphasizing physical key hardware. AppLocale picks the term buyers recognize on each screenshot — a Settings walkthrough needs 安全密钥-friendly phrasing; a YubiKey product headline may use 安全金钥 when accurate to your English source.

添加安全密钥 (Add Security Key)

US pages use "Add Security Key" or "Register your FIDO key." China storefront copy uses 添加安全密钥 on frames that walk buyers through the registration sheet. Do not substitute 创建通行密钥 (Create a passkey) — that is Passkey vocabulary, not Security Key registration.

Apple ID 安全密钥 (Apple ID Security Keys)

When your English subtitle or description says "Apple ID Security Keys" as a product category, zh-Hans buyers search Apple ID 安全密钥 or FIDO 安全密钥. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope — hardware second factor for Apple ID sign-in, not app-level WebAuthn login unless your English source genuinely markets both separately.

安全密钥 vs 六位验证码 (Security Key vs six-digit code)

Security Keys replace the six-digit verification code or trusted-device prompt with a physical key tap on new-device Apple ID sign-in. zh-Hans marketing may contrast 安全密钥 or 添加安全密钥 with 六位验证码 or 受信任设备 approval — accurate to Apple's hardware-key story, not the SMS or trusted-device 2FA flow as your lead claim, and not Passkey (通行密钥) vocabulary.

AppLocale FAQ

What are Apple ID Security Keys and why does listing copy matter?

Security Keys are physical FIDO2 hardware registered under Settings → Sign-In & Security → Two-Factor Authentication → Security Keys. Buyers add at least two keys and can tap a key on new-device Apple ID sign-in instead of a six-digit code or trusted-device approval.
